questions.text_english:
(1) Gossip. All humans partake in some form, despite the age-old adage, If you have nothing nice to say, don't say anything at all. Whether it's workplace chatter, the sharing of family news or group texts between friends, it's inevitable that anyone who participates in the above, talks about other people.

(2) People tend to think of gossip as synonymous with malicious rumours, put-downs, or the breathless propagation of a tabloid scoop. But researchers often define it more broadly as talking about people who aren't present,says an assistant professor of psychology. It's something that comes very naturally to us an integral part of conversation, information sharing, and even community building.

(3) It's not necessarily negative,adds a professor of psychology. It can be positive or neutral. Some researchers argue that gossip helped our ancestors survive. Evolutionary psychologists first pioneered this idea, comparing gossip to the grooming primates engage in as a means of bonding.

(4) People are usually resistant to thinking about gossip as anything but bad. It is true that there are some types of gossip that should be avoided, such as gossip that is purely harmful and serves no purpose like mean comments on someone's way of dressing. In such a scenario no one benefits. Gossip can also be both active and passive. Active gossiping refers to directly sharing negative information about someone else. An active gossiper initiates the conversation and actively spreads it. Passive gossiping on the other hand involves more subtle behaviour like hinting, dropping suggestive comments or participating in gossip by listening without actively contributing, but still allowing the gossip to spread through their presence.

(5) It's interesting to note that gossiping also says something about relationships people have with one another. The act of gossiping often implies a level of trust and closeness with someone, which are key aspects of a good friendship.

(6) Research has found that gossip can stave off loneliness, while other studies have found it can facilitate bonding and closeness and serve as a form of entertainment. So, keep on talking. And when your conversation turns to gossip, as it inevitably will, remember that some good can come of it - with the right intentions, of course.

sub_questions.text_english: By the phrase 'put-downs' the writer means _______.
sub_questions.solution: The writer uses 'put-downs' to mean belittling or critical comments made to lower the esteem of others.

sub_questions.text_english: Despite the bad reputation of 'gossip', mention any two benefits that it offers.
sub_questions.solution: Two benefits of gossip are that it facilitates social bonding and closeness, and it serves as a form of entertainment that can help stave off loneliness.

sub_questions.text_english: The concern this phrase ('It's something that comes very naturally to us') points towards is about A. that some types of gossip should be avoided. B. that gossip can be viewed as part of our daily interaction and bonding.

options.A: that some types of gossip should be avoided.
options.B: that gossip can be viewed as part of our daily interaction and bonding.

sub_questions.solution: Option B is correct because the phrase highlights gossip's role as an integral, innate part of human communication and community building, rather than just a malicious act.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the analogy with one word from paragraph (2). Praise: Commend :: _______ : Malevolent (A) Scoop (B) Propagation (C) Malicious (D) Conversation
sub_questions.solution: The analogy is based on synonyms. 'Malicious' is the synonym for 'Malevolent' found in the paragraph.

sub_questions.text_english: What type of gossip does the author disapprove of and why?
sub_questions.solution: The author disapproves of gossip that is purely harmful, such as mean comments about someone's appearance, because it serves no constructive purpose and benefits no one.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the following suitably with one difference between the author's opinion and that of people about gossip.
sub_questions.solution: Generally, people think of gossip as synonymous with malicious rumors, whereas the author views it broadly as talking about those not present, which can be neutral or positive.

sub_questions.text_english: Based on the statement about active and passive gossip, classify: Sentence 1: Ranjan told Raman and Shah the sensational facts he had heard about his friend Vineet from others. Sentence 2: Kumar stayed silent while his friends criticized his close friend Vijay in his absence.
sub_questions.solution: Sentence 1 is active participation because the person initiates and shares the information, and Sentence 2 is passive participation because the person allows gossip to spread through their silent presence.

sub_questions.text_english: Why does the author say that gossip is a reflection of relationships?
sub_questions.solution: The author says this because the act of gossiping often implies a level of trust and closeness between individuals, which are essential elements of a good friendship.

sub_questions.text_english: The statement that gossip can 'stave off loneliness' is true as: (A) we always enjoy talking ill of others. (B) we believe what we read about people in the print media. (C) we are free to talk loosely in the absence of the person. (D) in order to gossip, you need to feel close to people.

options.A: we always enjoy talking ill of others.
options.B: we believe what we read about people in the print media.
options.C: we are free to talk loosely in the absence of the person.
options.D: in order to gossip, you need to feel close to people.

sub_questions.solution: Option D is correct as gossiping creates a bond and fosters closeness between people, thereby reducing feelings of loneliness.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the following: The author puts forth the fact that man can never _______ gossiping.
sub_questions.solution: The sentence is completed as: The author puts forth the fact that man can never stop gossiping, as it is inevitable.

questions.text_english:
(1) Introduction: Humans are social creatures with a deep desire to interact with one another. Recent developments in technology have made it possible for billions of people worldwide to use cell phones to satisfy this need. The current study aims to analyse the impact of smartphone use among various categories of people in Kerala, India. The present study will provide an insight into the extent and magnitude of people's reliance on smartphones to communicate in this modern age and the dwindling nature of social relationships.

(2) Methodology: A google form created questionnaire was used to gather information on the subject from a sample of participants who were from various districts in Kerala, India.

(3) Survey Examination: Among the 131 study participants, 66 were men and the remaining 65 were women. For convenience, the study considered only the main purpose for which a smartphone is used by any given individual.

(4) Results: 
S.No | Purpose | Frequency | Percentage
1. | Academic | 21 | 11-11
2. | Communication | 56 | 29-63
3. | Entertainment | 48 | 25-40
4. | Others | 64 | 33-86
Individuals differed in their interests and preferences regarding their choice of communication medium. Some preferred direct conversation, while others conveyed their messages through virtual mediums of communication, that did not involve any face-to-face interaction.

(5) Implications for Interventions: It was observed that individuals were interested in using their smartphones even when they were dining. This constant use can have several disadvantages such as reckless use of mobile phones, including prolonged hours of radiation exposure, over-calorie intake due to binge eating, leading to obesity, and other health problems. It is also a vital tool to achieve social progress. The use of phones while travelling can sometimes detract from an individual's enjoyment of the serenity of the environment, the scenic beauty of picnic spots, and affect the way an individual behaves and interacts with his or her co-travellers.

(6) Conclusion: It is true that most of the population under different age and gender categories use smartphones every day, but there is no significant fall in the duration spent in direct face-to-face conversation with fellow beings, except in very few individuals. The majority of people agree that traditional face-to-face communication is more comfortable, reliable, and expressive than text messages, phone calls, or electronic mail.

sub_questions.text_english: In paragraph (1), the author highlights the use of smartphones to _______.

fill_values: satisfy the human desire to interact

sub_questions.solution: The author highlights that technology enables humans to satisfy their deep-rooted social need to interact with others worldwide.

sub_questions.text_english: How does the author validate the fact that smartphones take away the joy of beauty around us?
sub_questions.solution: The author validates this by noting that phone use while traveling can detract from enjoying the serenity of the environment and scenic beauty of picnic spots.

sub_questions.text_english: Classify the following sentences as direct and virtual communication: Sentence 1: Most of the students attend online classes on mobile phones. Sentence 2: He arranged for a get-together to meet his school friends.
sub_questions.solution: Sentence 1 is virtual communication as it happens via a digital interface, and Sentence 2 is direct communication as it involves face-to-face interaction.

sub_questions.text_english: In paragraph (5), 'By reckless use of mobile phones' the author blames: (A) binge eating (B) mobile phones (C) responsibility of man (D) demands of society
sub_questions.solution: The author blames the 'responsibility of man' (the user) for the reckless usage that leads to health and social issues.

sub_questions.text_english: Give two points to support how smartphones make a major impact on man's life.
sub_questions.solution: Smartphones impact life by serving as a vital tool for social progress and modern communication, while simultaneously causing health issues like obesity from binge eating and distracting people from their immediate environment.

sub_questions.text_english: There is no significant fall in the duration spent in direct face-to-face conversation. Select the appropriate response: (A) Primary purpose (B) Secondary objective (C) Method of analysis (D) Research outcome
sub_questions.solution: This finding, derived from the study's observation of participant habits, constitutes a research outcome.

sub_questions.text_english: Technological development is a double-edged sword.' Analyse the above statement with reference to the text.
sub_questions.solution: Technology is a 'double-edged sword' because, while it provides a vital tool for communication and social progress, it simultaneously fosters health risks like radiation and obesity and diminishes the quality of real-life social interactions.

sub_questions.text_english: The study is very relevant in the contemporary times, because: (A) we are living in the 21st century. (B) it is an era of IT revolution. (C) mobile phones have penetrated everyone's life. (D) mobile phones are used by students for academic purposes.

options.A: we are living in the 21st century.
options.B: it is an era of IT revolution.
options.C: mobile phones have penetrated everyone's life.
options.D: mobile phones are used by students for academic purposes.

sub_questions.solution: The study's findings are universally applicable because mobile phone usage has become pervasive in every individual's daily life.

questions.text_english: (a) In today's fast-paced world, fitness apps have become a popular tool for tracking and improving health. Write an article for your school magazine educating the youth on the pros and cons of fitness apps. You are Kirti/Kirat, a school fitness coach. OR (b) You are Ritika/Ritik of Class XII-D and a member of the school editorial board. Write a comprehensive report detailing the activities undertaken by students as part of Cyber Safety Awareness Week.
questions.solution:
PROS AND CONS OF FITNESS APPS
By Kirti, School Fitness Coach

In our increasingly digital world, fitness apps have emerged as a dominant trend. They are popular because they offer convenience, personalized workout routines, and real-time tracking of physical activity. These apps monitor health metrics like heart rate, calories burned, and sleep quality, motivating users to stay active. However, blind reliance on these tools has downsides. Often, users lack the professional guidance required to perform exercises safely, leading to injuries. Furthermore, these apps collect vast amounts of sensitive personal data, raising significant privacy and security concerns. The focus on numbers can also encourage obsessive behavior and unhealthy competition. Fitness apps should be used judiciously as a supplement to, not a replacement for, professional coaching and intuitive self-awareness. By integrating them with a balanced diet and expert advice, we can use technology effectively to foster a healthier lifestyle.

questions.text_english: (a) Aunt Jennifer's fingers fluttering through her wool / Find even the ivory needle hard to pull... (Aunt Jennifer's Tigers) OR (b) Driving from my parent's / home to Cochin last Friday / morning, I saw my mother, / beside me, / doze, open mouthed, her face / ashen like that / of a corpse... (My Mother at Sixty-six)

sub_questions.text_english: The massive weight of 'wedding band' symbolises _______.
sub_questions.solution: The wedding band symbolizes the heavy, restrictive, and often traumatic burden of Aunt Jennifer's unhappy married life, which dominates her existence.

sub_questions.text_english: By the phrase 'fingers fluttering', the poet portrays Aunt Jennifer in a constant state of (nervousness/happiness).
sub_questions.solution: The word 'fluttering' portrays her extreme nervousness and anxiety, likely caused by her oppressive marriage.

sub_questions.text_english: Assertion: Aunt Jennifer lives a life full of agony and pain. Reason: She is a victim of the male dominant society. Choose the correct option...

options.A: Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.
options.B: Both the assertion and the reason are true, but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion.
options.C: The assertion is true, but the reason is false.
options.D: The assertion is false, but the reason is true.

sub_questions.solution: The reason directly explains the agony Aunt Jennifer experiences as she struggles under the weight of an oppressive, patriarchal marriage.

sub_questions.text_english: The tigers in the panel will go on prancing.............. The above line refers to the _______ of art.
sub_questions.solution: The line refers to the immortality of art, as the creations Aunt Jennifer made will survive long after she is gone.

sub_questions.text_english: The expressions 'terrified hands' and 'ordeals' used in the above extract highlight the _______ of women in marriage.
sub_questions.solution: These words highlight the deep-seated oppression and the psychological struggle women often face within restrictive, patriarchal marriages.

sub_questions.text_english: Tigers in the panel' symbolise (A) Aunt Jennifer's interest in wildlife. (B) Tigers in the green forest. (C) Aunt Jennifer's deep desire for freedom. (D) Tigers that are yellow in colour.

options.C: Aunt Jennifer's deep desire for freedom.
options.D: Tigers that are yellow in colour.

sub_questions.solution: The tigers represent the freedom, confidence, and strength that Aunt Jennifer secretly aspires to possess, contrasting with her own timid reality.

questions.text_english: (a) That young master is so proud of his skill to save life that he saves any life,the cook said contemptuously... (The Enemy) OR (b) The British officer's secretary sent word to the Maharaja through the dewan that the durai himself did not have to kill the tiger... (The Tiger King)
questions.solution: The cook's tone is one of contempt, as he believes Dr. Sadao's medical pride has led him to make the reckless decision of saving an enemy soldier, a man who is legally a traitor. This highlights the servant's narrow-minded patriotism and his disapproval of the doctor's humanitarian choice, which he feels will endanger the family.

questions.text_english: (a) Those were the days of mainly indoor shooting, and only five percent of the film was shot outdoors... (Poets and Pancakes) OR (b) My Last French Lesson! Why, I hardly knew how to write! I should never learn any more! I must stop there, then!... (The Last Lesson)
questions.solution: By 'indoor shooting', the writer means that filming was done primarily inside studio sets with artificial, controlled lighting rather than on actual outdoor locations. This setup was common during the period described at Gemini Studios, where the focus was on studio-based production techniques.

sub_questions.text_english: Why does M. Hamel refer to language as a key to freedom from slavery?
sub_questions.solution: M. Hamel emphasizes that a language is a repository of a nation's identity and culture. When a people are enslaved, as long as they hold fast to their language, it is as if they possess the key to their prison, allowing them to preserve their national dignity and eventually secure freedom.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain how Mukesh in 'Lost Spring' stands as a ray of hope for the bangle making community.
sub_questions.solution: Mukesh stands as a ray of hope because, unlike the resigned elders in Firozabad, he dares to dream beyond his caste-based occupation. His ambition to become a motor mechanic shows an independent spirit and a refusal to be trapped in the cycle of poverty, signaling potential change.

sub_questions.text_english: What is the importance of beauty in a man's life?
sub_questions.solution: Beauty is essential because it provides solace and motivation. It acts as a permanent balm that removes the pall of despondency from our lives, inspiring us to keep moving forward despite the suffering and ugliness that often define the human experience.

sub_questions.text_english: How did Umberto Eco display his innovative style in the presentation of his dissertation?
sub_questions.solution: Umberto Eco presented his dissertation in a highly narrative, storytelling style. Instead of a dry, academic delivery, he shared his trial-and-error process, including his mistakes, which transformed a traditional academic work into a vivid and engaging account of intellectual discovery.

sub_questions.text_english: What is Robert Frost's complaint in 'A Roadside Stand'?
sub_questions.solution: Robert Frost complains about the indifference of the city-dwelling elite toward the rural poor. He highlights the pathetic condition of the roadside stand owners who wait in vain for the 'polished traffic' to stop and buy their goods, exposing the widening economic gap in society.

sub_questions.text_english: What was the link between the makeup department and national integration as described in 'Poets and Pancakes'?
sub_questions.solution: The makeup department served as a unique example of national integration because its staff were drawn from different parts of India, including a Bengali, a Maharashtrian, a Dharwar Kannadiga, an Andhraite, and a Madras Christian. They worked together harmoniously, exemplifying national unity.

sub_questions.text_english: How was the 'Students on Ice' programme significant in giving an awakening call to the younger generation?
sub_questions.solution: The program provided students with a firsthand experience of the Antarctic environment and the visible impacts of global warming. This served as an awakening call, urging them to recognize the fragility of our ecosystem and inspiring them to take responsibility for Earth's future.

sub_questions.text_english: What did Charley realize when he saw an issue of the newspaper 'The World'?
sub_questions.solution: When Charley saw an issue of 'The World' newspaper dated June 11, 1894, he realized he had successfully traveled back in time to the past, confirming the existence of the Third Level, which he had previously only imagined.

sub_questions.text_english: 'Success is the best revenge.' How did Zitkala-Sa stand as a testimony to the above statement in 'Memories of Childhood'?
sub_questions.solution: Zitkala-Sa faced immense cultural oppression at the Carlisle Indian School. She fought to preserve her identity and eventually achieved academic excellence. Her success as a writer and activist served as a powerful testimony, reclaiming the voice that the educational system had tried to silence.

questions.text_english: Answer any one of the following two questions in 120-150 words: (a) How do the characters of Rajkumar Shukla from 'Indigo' and William Douglas from 'Deep Water' compare and contrast in terms of their courage, constraints, and determination? OR (b) Analyse the lesson 'Lost Spring' and the poem 'A Roadside Stand' with reference to social inequality and the indifferent attitude of society.
questions.solution:
Rajkumar Shukla and William Douglas are powerful examples of determination, though they operated under vastly different constraints. Shukla’s courage was rooted in his unyielding commitment to the cause of the sharecroppers. He was a simple, illiterate peasant whose primary constraint was his lack of resources and social standing. Yet, his unwavering determination to get Gandhi to Champaran forced the hands of the colonial authorities, illustrating that persistence can overcome formidable political barriers. 

In contrast, William Douglas was constrained by an irrational, internal fear of drowning. His determination was channeled into a disciplined, long-term effort to master his phobia through swimming lessons. While Shukla fought for a community's rights, Douglas fought for personal survival and the recovery of his confidence. Both men share a refusal to yield to their respective limitations, demonstrating that whether the struggle is personal or communal, relentless perseverance is the key to achieving one's goals and securing justice.

questions.text_english: Answer any one of the following two questions in 120-150 words: (a) In what way did Mr. Lamb's ideas of watching, listening, and thinking help Derry change his perspective towards life? OR (b) According to Tishani Doshi in 'Journey to the end of the Earth', man's supremacy over nature is responsible for the problems we face today. Support your answer with evidence from the text.
questions.solution:
Mr. Lamb's philosophy of watching, listening, and thinking plays a pivotal role in transforming Derry’s life. Derry enters the garden filled with self-pity and bitterness due to his facial disfigurement. Mr. Lamb, despite his own disability, remains vibrant and optimistic, teaching Derry that life is about more than just a physical appearance. By encouraging Derry to watch the world around him, listen to the sounds of nature, and think deeply about his perceptions, Lamb challenges Derry’s defensive mindset.

He shows Derry that beauty is subjective and that his disability need not define his identity. Derry learns that he can choose how he interacts with the world. Through Lamb’s gentle guidance and philosophical wisdom, Derry realizes that he is not a prisoner of his circumstances. He begins to see the potential for joy and connection, eventually finding the courage to return to the garden, signaling a fundamental shift from self-loathing to self-acceptance and a newfound appreciation for the richness of existence.
